newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Iscor falls on poor results, profit warning.
newsitem.headline: Iscor falls on poor results, profit warning.

text.p: South African steel producer Iscor slid 2.55 percent after trading more than two million shares, dragged down by poor results and a profit warning for the first half of the current financial year, dealers said.
By 0833 GMT the share had lost seven cents to 2.68 rand and dealer saw it falling further with a bottom at 2.50-2.55 rand.
"More than two million shares have changed hands on the back of poor reaction in the market to the results and we see further weakness," one dealer said.
Asked how far the share could fall, another dealer said: "We see a likely bottom at around 2.55 or 2.50 rand."
Posting results for the year ended June 30, Iscor made 35.7 cents per share after exceptional items from 36.4 cents previously. It held its dividend steady at 16.5 cents a share.
Iscor Ltd said it saw no immediate prospect of the domestic steel market improving and warned that profits in the first half of the 1996/97 year would be well down on a year ago.
